papers.title: Characterizing charge-parity detection based on an offset-charge-tunable transmon qubit via randomized benchmarking
papers.abstract: Superconducting qubits are compelling platforms for charge-parity detection and, due to their theoretical sensitivity on the meV energy scale, hold promise for rare event searches. In this work, we realize high-fidelity mapping of charge-parity states onto qubit states using an offset-charge-tunable transmon qubit and efficiently characterize the fidelity of the charge-parity detection via randomized benchmarking. Specifically, a gate control line is applied to control offset charge, allowing us to achieve the single-qubit gate fidelity up to 99.96%. We combine a net-zero-based pulse on the gate line with a spin-echo-based sequence to realize charge-parity mapping, achieving a fidelity of 99.37%. Then, we demonstrate continuous monitoring of the charge-parity state with over 93.4% fidelity at a 4-μs sampling interval. Finally, an error analysis of charge-parity detection is performed, and it is found that qubit readout is currently the largest source of error. We believe this work lays the foundation for future exploration of ultra-low energy particles.

summary.summary: This work demonstrates high-fidelity charge-parity detection using an offset-charge-tunable transmon qubit with a gate control line, achieving single-qubit gate fidelity of 99.96% and charge-parity mapping fidelity of 99.37% via a spin-echo-based sequence (EchoCPM) with net-zero gate pulses. Continuous monitoring of charge-parity state reaches 93.4% fidelity at 4 μs sampling, with qubit readout identified as the primary error source limiting detection performance.
summary.motivation: Superconducting qubits exhibit meV-scale sensitivity to quasiparticle generation from cosmic rays and other low-energy events, making them promising for rare-event detection schemes like quantum parity detectors. Prior Ramsey-based charge-parity detection achieved only 91–92% fidelity; a more robust protocol with quantitative benchmarking via randomized benchmarking was lacking.
summary.method: An asymmetric Josephson junction transmon qubit on a flip-chip architecture with separate microwave/flux and gate control lines was used. Charge-parity mapping combined a spin-echo sequence ($X/2$-$X$-$Y/2$) with opposite-sign net-zero gate pulses (amplitude 0.67 V, duration 217 ns) to accumulate $\pi$ phase difference between even and odd parity states. Gate-pulse duration was calibrated using interleaved randomized benchmarking. Continuous detection fidelity was characterized via power spectral density fitting of random-telegraph-signal quasiparticle tunneling data.
summary.result: Interleaved RB yielded pseudo-$Z$ gate fidelity 98.91% and combined charge-parity mapping fidelity $99.45\% \times 99.95\% \times 99.97\% = 99.37\%$. Continuous detection over 30 s with 4 μs sampling gave $F_{\mathrm{eff}} = 93.4\%$, compared to calculated $F_{\mathrm{eff}} = 94.0\%$ with measured $F_g = 99.5\%$, $F_e = 95.1\%$; measured quasiparticle-tunneling time $\tau = 30.2$ ms. Readout fidelity imbalance limits overall detection fidelity.
